turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_fatigue_train.csv: 293 real samples, columns process/composition
    columns (NT, THT, THt, THQCr, CT, Ct, DT, Dt, QmT, TT, Tt, TCr, C, Si,
    Mn, P, S, Ni, Cr, Cu, Mo, RedRatio, dA, dB, dC) and `target` (the
    measured rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa)).
  - b3_fatigue_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE samples whose rotating-bending
    fatigue strength (MPa) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and the
    same process/composition columns.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST rotating-
bending fatigue strength (MPa), then select the 5 best candidates from the
pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
I focused on training clusters with the highest fatigue strength. The 930-series case-hardened/heat-treated samples dominate the upper range (many >1000 MPa), while most other process groups are below ~650 MPa.

Using nearest training analogs and adjusting for tempering/case-depth effects:
- `c081` is closest to the strongest training sample (1144 MPa) but with a slightly less favorable tempering condition.
- `c063` and `c018` are from a high-strength 930-series composition group; `c063` has the deeper-case/lower-tempering benefit, while `c018` is slightly downgraded by higher tempering.
- `c053` is from the composition group that reached 1110 MPa in training, though its lower carburizing time reduces it somewhat.
- `c016` is from the 1082 MPa training composition, with a less favorable tempering condition.

Final: c081, c063, c018, c053, c016
